stories.headline: Nvidia commits $1B over five years to US science and quantum R&D under Genesis Mission

key_facts.fact: On October 8, 2026, at a Washington event, Nvidia announced commitments valued at $1 billion over the next five years to build out US capacity for 'super intelligence' R&D in quantum computing, healthcare and energy security.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA today announced commitments valued at $1 billion to build out the United States' capacity for super intelligence research and development in fields critical for U.S. leadership, including quantum computing, healthcare and energy security.

key_facts.fact: The money will go to higher-education research institutions, investments in US quantum leadership, and cloud service providers serving US government missions.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA will commit $1 billion to the advancement of super intelligence for science and quantum computing across the U.S. through support of the nation's higher-education research institutions, investments in accelerating American quantum leadership and support for cloud service providers bolstering U.S. government mission needs.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang said: 'President Trump's Genesis Mission is launching a new golden age of American discovery... With a $1 billion investment, NVIDIA is putting advanced Super Intelligence in the hands of America's scientists.'
key_facts.excerpt: "President Trump's Genesis Mission is launching a new golden age of American discovery," said Jensen Huang... "With a $1 billion investment, NVIDIA is putting advanced Super Intelligence in the hands of America's scientists to accelerate breakthroughs in medicine, energy and materials."

key_facts.fact: The Department of Energy separately announced $159 million for 12 Phase 2 Genesis Mission projects, several with Nvidia as collaborator, covering quantum computing, fusion, accelerator design and microelectronics.
key_facts.excerpt: The DOE separately announced $159 million in funding for 12 new Phase 2 Genesis Mission projects. The projects include work on an AI-enabled digital twin for Commonwealth Fusion Systems' SPARC fusion device and the design of rugged microchips.

key_facts.fact: The Register put the commitment at about 1/60th of Nvidia's quarterly profit and noted Nvidia is building seven new supercomputers for Argonne and Los Alamos, including the 100,000-Blackwell-GPU Solstice system at Argonne.
key_facts.excerpt: commit $1 billion — about 1/60th of its quarterly profits... Argonne will house the 100,000 Blackwell-GPU-based Solstice system.

key_facts.fact: At the same White House summit, President Trump awarded the National Medal of Science to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD CEO Lisa Su, alongside Elon Musk and Sergey Brin.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump joined Michael Kratsios to award the Medal of Science to Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Lisa Su and Sergey Brin amid announcements about new science funding.

stories.headline: Nvidia-backed Firmus pulls A$44B ASX IPO, explores $2B-$3B private round instead

key_facts.fact: Australian AI data-center developer Firmus withdrew its application to list on the ASX on Friday, October 9, citing 'recent market volatility and prevailing market conditions'.
key_facts.excerpt: The company, which counts chip giant Nvidia as a backer, announced on Friday it had decided to withdraw its application to list on the Australian Securities Exchange, citing "recent market volatility and prevailing market conditions".

key_facts.fact: Firmus had sought up to A$7.9 billion ($5.5 billion) at A$11 a share, a market value of about A$43.9 billion ($30.7 billion), which would have been Australia's second-largest IPO after Telstra in 1997.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus aimed to raise up to $7.9 billion Australian dollars ($5.5 billion), setting its offer at AU$11 per share, which would have resulted in a market valuation of AU$43.9 billion ($30.7 billion), making it the second-largest Australian IPO after the listing of government telecommunications giant Telstra in 1997.

key_facts.fact: Before pulling the float, Firmus first cut its asking price and then considered making the terms friendlier to investors.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus first cut the share price it was asking for, then considered making the terms of the deal friendlier to investors, and finally pulled the float altogether on Friday morning.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported Firmus and its advisers are in talks with existing investors to raise $2 billion to $3 billion privately, possibly mixing equity and debt; it is unclear whether Nvidia would participate.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus and its financial advisers are holding discussions with current investors about assembling the private round... options on the table that could blend equity and debt instruments. It is unclear whether Nvidia $NVDA would participate.

key_facts.fact: Firmus has raised more than $3 billion in equity over the past year from backers including Nvidia, Coatue and Blackstone, which extended $10 billion in debt financing in February; the AFR reported it is now looking at a Nasdaq listing.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus has undertaken several equity raises over the past year, bringing in more than $3 billion... Nvidia has participated in the fundraising, along with tech investor Coatue and private equity giant Blackstone, which in February extended $10 billion in debt financing... it is now looking to list on the Nasdaq exchange in the U.S.

key_facts.fact: Firmus plans a $51 billion build of five AI data centers over the next two years.
key_facts.excerpt: it will now look at "other options" for its $51 billion build of five AI data centres over the next two years.

stories.headline: Apple cuts iPhone 18 Pro component orders 15-20% as memory-driven price hikes dent demand

key_facts.fact: Apple told some suppliers to cut production of components for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max after soaring memory-chip costs forced price increases that dampened demand, Nikkei Asia reported on October 9.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple has told some of its suppliers to cut production of components for its newly launched iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, after soaring memory chip costs forced price increases that have dampened consumer demand.

key_facts.fact: Component orders for October were cut by 15% to 20% from what was originally expected.
key_facts.excerpt: component orders for October being cut by 15%-20% from what was originally expected, the Nikkei reported.

key_facts.fact: The new Pro models are at least 10% pricier than their predecessors, so the cuts may not immediately hit revenue; the standard iPhone 18 was pushed to early 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The production cuts may not immediately translate into lower revenue for Apple because the new models are at least 10% more expensive than their predecessors... the standard iPhone 18 and the next-generation iPhone Air are expected to arrive in spring 2027.

key_facts.fact: TrendForce estimates the memory cost in a 256GB iPhone 18 Pro rose nearly 400% year over year, with memory now 34% of the phone's component cost versus 10% before.
key_facts.excerpt: The estimated cost of memory in the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro has surged nearly 400% year over year, according to TrendForce. Memory now accounts for 34% of the phone's component costs, up from just 10%.

key_facts.fact: The report raised concerns about Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, which starts at $1,999 and goes on sale later in October; IDC expects global smartphone shipments to fall 16.7% in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: the iPhone Duo, which starts at $1,999... is set to go on sale later this month... IDC expects global smartphone shipments to fall 16.7% in 2026, marking the industry's largest year-on-year decline.

stories.headline: IDC: global PC shipments plunge 20.1% in Q3 to 62.7M as memory-driven price hikes bite

key_facts.fact: Worldwide PC shipments fell 20.1% year over year in Q3 2026 to 62.7 million units, per IDC preliminary data released October 8; the second straight decline, deeper than Q2's 3.8% drop.
key_facts.excerpt: Worldwide PC shipments fell 20.1% year over year in Q3 2026 to 62.7 million units... the second consecutive decline and a deeper one than the 3.8% drop in Q2.

key_facts.fact: Shipments also fell 9.1% from Q2, breaking the usual seasonal pattern, because vendors and channels pulled in inventory earlier in the year ahead of memory-driven price hikes.
key_facts.excerpt: Shipments also slipped 9.1% sequentially... the inventory pull-in earlier in the year, as vendors and channels rushed to stock up ahead of memory-driven price hikes, left the quarter with little demand to draw on.

key_facts.fact: IDC lists higher price points driven by the AI data-center buildout as a primary driver of the decline.
key_facts.excerpt: Primary drivers of the decline: Strategic inventory pull-in across the entire industry as a result of on-going supply constraints and higher price points driven by AI data center build out

key_facts.fact: IDC's Jitesh Ubrani said prices will remain elevated and the outlook could worsen with deteriorating macro conditions.
key_facts.excerpt: "...we don't expect pricing anywhere near what it was a year ago. Prices will remain elevated. With macro conditions worsening, the risk is that the outlook for the next few quarters gets worse before it gets better."

sources.title: PC Market Woes Continue: Shipments Fall 20.1% in Q3 2026 as Pull-In Hangover and Supply Constraints Bite

stories.headline: Warehouse 'robots-as-a-service' startup Ultra raises $62M, deepens Physical Intelligence tie-up

key_facts.fact: Brooklyn-based Ultra, which leases packing robots to warehouses for a monthly fee, announced on Friday, October 9, that it has raised $62 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Ultra, a startup that leases its devices to warehouses under a monthly "robots as a service" model... On Friday, the Brooklyn-based company announced it had raised $62 million

key_facts.fact: The funding comprises a $50 million Series A led by Framework Ventures with Y Combinator participating, and an earlier $12 million seed led by Y Combinator and Next View.
key_facts.excerpt: a $50 million Series A led by Framework Ventures with participation from Y Combinator, and an earlier $12 million seed round led by the latter and Next View.

key_facts.fact: Ultra says its robots have packed more than half a million orders for shipping in US warehouses.
key_facts.excerpt: according to the company, the devices have packed more than half a million orders for shipping.

key_facts.fact: Ultra builds and installs the robots but relies on Physical Intelligence, valued at $5.6 billion, for the AI 'brains'; the two companies deepened their partnership.
key_facts.excerpt: Ultra builds and installs the robots, but relies on Physical Intelligence to supply the AI... PI, which is valued at $5.6 billion

key_facts.fact: Customers pay an upfront integration fee plus a monthly support fee; CEO Jon Miller Schwartz says demand has let Ultra raise prices, and that humanoids are about five years from similar scaling.
key_facts.excerpt: clients pay an up-front integration fee for Ultra to install the robots, and then an ongoing monthly fee... Ultra has been able to raise prices... Schwartz says give it five years.

sources.title: Ultra raises $62 million for fast-growing 'robots as a service' business, announces tie-up with AI research firm Physical Intelligence

stories.headline: Sabi raises $50M for thought-to-text BCI cap built on its own TSMC-fabbed sensor chip

key_facts.fact: Palo Alto-based Sabi raised $50 million to build a baseball cap with 100,000 sensors that converts neural signals into text prompts for AI agents, Forbes reported on October 9.
key_facts.excerpt: Palo Alto-based Sabi is betting its cap, outfitted with 100,000 sensors, will enable people to talk to their AI agents just by thinking.

key_facts.fact: Investors include Khosla Ventures, Accel, Initialized, DST Global and former OpenAI executive Kevin Weil.
key_facts.excerpt: we've raised $50M from Khosla Ventures, Accel, Initialized, Kevin Weil, DST Global to build the world's most wearable BCI cap at Sabi

key_facts.fact: CEO Rahul Chhabra said Sabi built non-contact neuro-sensors that read signals through hair, and that TSMC helped fabricate what he called the world's first chip purpose-built for consumer BCI.
key_facts.excerpt: we have built non-contact neuro-sensors that can capture reliable signals even through hair... thanks to TSMC for helping fabricate the world's first chip purpose-built for consumer BCI

key_facts.fact: The device is non-invasive, unlike implanted brain-computer interfaces.
key_facts.excerpt: Sabi, a Palo Alto startup, has raised $50 million to build a wearable brain-computer interface that converts thoughts into prompts. The device is a beanie, not a brain implant.
